subject: Geopolitics
title: Counterintelligence
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Counterintelligence.

hook.text: Kim Philby was head of anti-Soviet operations at MI6. He was a Soviet spy the entire time. Decades of work — wasted.

buildup.text: Counterintelligence means catching enemy spies, protecting your secrets, and rooting out moles within your own ranks.

discovery.text: The hardest part isn't finding foreign spies. It's suspecting your own colleagues — people you trust with your life.

twist.text: Paranoia is occupational. James Angleton at the CIA suspected so many people that his mole hunts paralyzed the agency.

climax.text: Counterintelligence is a hall of mirrors. You never know if the mole you caught was the only one.

punchline.text: The enemy you can't see is the one sitting beside you.

quiz.question: Who was Kim Philby?
options: A CIA analyst who leaked files to China
A senior MI6 officer secretly working for the Soviet Union
A KGB defector who exposed Soviet spy networks
